body.statement: Almost surely, the constrained and unconstrained GCM slopes differ only on a finite contact interval at every \(x\), the integral \(D(x)\) is finite and nonnegative, and \(D\) has a separable locally bounded stationary version. Moreover, the joint contact radius for all \(x\) in a bounded interval has a tail sufficient for independent truncation of well-separated Brownian blocks.
body.justification: The continuum maximum and any declustering rule are meaningful only after the nonlocal GCM energy is localized and given a separable version.
body.gap: Banerjee and Wellner (2001) prove the one-point LR integral is well defined; the uniform contact-radius and local-boundedness statement for the translated field is not supplied there.
body.consumer: Finite-dimensional stationarity is available, while simulation and block separation still need separability and a quantitative common contact-radius tail.

obligation.what_is_open: A separable locally bounded version and a quantitative common contact-radius tail over every compact set of constraint locations have not been constructed.
obligation.obstruction: Parabolic drift localizes individual variational pictures, but an argmin tail does not control every remote supporting chord for both one-sided constrained GCMs uniformly over a continuum. The target also does not quantify the tail strength it calls sufficient.
obligation.attempted: Brownian translation and affine GCM equivariance prove exact finite-dimensional stationarity. Attempts to upgrade an individual argmin bound stop at the uncontrolled remote-chord event.
obligation.partial_result:
Whenever the two GCM energies are defined, their finite-dimensional stationarity is exact.  For \(x,t\in\mathbb R\), set
\[
 \mathbb W_x(t)=\mathbb W(x+t)-\mathbb W(x).
\]
Then
\[
 X(x+t)-X(x)-2xt=\mathbb W_x(t)+t^2.
\]
Affine equivariance of greatest convex minorants and the change of variable \(s=x+t\) therefore give
\[
 D(x)=\Phi(\mathbb W_x),
\]
where \(\Phi\) is the origin-constrained Brownian--GCM energy.  Stationarity of Brownian increments yields, for every \(m\ge1\), every \(x_1,\ldots,x_m,h\in\mathbb R\),
\[
 (\mathbb W_{x_1+h},\ldots,\mathbb W_{x_m+h})
 \stackrel{d}{=}
 (\mathbb W_{x_1},\ldots,\mathbb W_{x_m}),
\]
and hence translation invariance of the finite-dimensional distributions of \(D\).  This argument neither constructs a separable locally bounded modification nor bounds the joint contact radius over a continuum of constraint locations.  In particular, an individual argmin tail does not rule out a remote supporting chord that changes one of the two one-sided constrained GCMs.
